options.name: -iL
options.summary: Read targets from a file, one host/range per line.

options.name: --exclude
options.summary: Skip these hosts or networks (comma-separated).

options.name: --excludefile
options.summary: Skip the hosts listed in a file.

options.name: -sL
options.summary: List scan: list the targets (with reverse DNS) without sending them any packets.

options.name: -sn
options.summary: Ping scan: find which hosts are up, skip the port scan.

options.name: -Pn
options.summary: Skip host discovery and treat every target as up.
options.detail: Useful when hosts block pings, but every address gets a full port scan, so it's much slower on sparse ranges.

options.name: -PS
options.summary: TCP SYN ping to the given ports (default 80).
options.detail: Without root, nmap uses a full connect() instead of a raw SYN.

options.name: -PA
options.summary: TCP ACK ping to the given ports (default 80).
options.detail: Without root, nmap falls back to a connect()-based ping.

options.name: -PU
options.summary: UDP ping to the given ports (default 40125).

options.name: -PY
options.summary: SCTP INIT ping.

options.name: -PE
options.summary: ICMP echo (classic ping).

options.name: -PP
options.summary: ICMP timestamp ping; sometimes gets through when echo is filtered.

options.name: -PM
options.summary: ICMP address-mask ping.

options.name: -PO
options.summary: IP protocol ping (default ICMP, IGMP, IP-in-IP).

options.name: -PR
options.summary: ARP ping; the most reliable discovery on your own LAN.

options.name: --disable-arp-ping
options.summary: Don't use ARP/ND discovery on local networks.

options.name: --traceroute
options.summary: Trace the network path (hops) to each host.

options.name: -n
options.summary: Never do reverse DNS; faster, but no hostnames.

options.name: -R
options.summary: Always do reverse DNS, even for hosts that are down.

options.name: --dns-servers
options.summary: Use these DNS servers for reverse lookups.

options.name: --system-dns
options.summary: Use the operating system's resolver instead of nmap's own.

options.name: --resolve-all
options.summary: Scan every address a hostname resolves to, not just the first.

options.name: --discovery-ignore-rst
options.summary: Don't count a TCP RST as proof a host is up (for firewalls that forge them).

options.name: -sT
options.summary: TCP connect scan: full handshakes. The default without root.

options.name: -sS
options.summary: TCP SYN (half-open) scan: fast and quieter. The default as root.

options.name: -sU
options.summary: UDP scan (DNS, SNMP, DHCP…). Slow: closed UDP ports are rate-limited.

options.name: -sA
options.summary: ACK scan: maps firewall rules (filtered vs unfiltered), not open ports.

options.name: -sW
options.summary: Window scan: like ACK, but reads the TCP window to guess open ports on some systems.

options.name: -sM
options.summary: Maimon scan (FIN/ACK probe).

options.name: -sN
options.summary: TCP Null scan (no flags set); can slip past stateless firewalls.

options.name: -sF
options.summary: TCP FIN scan.

options.name: -sX
options.summary: TCP Xmas scan (FIN, PSH and URG set).

options.name: --scanflags
options.summary: Build a custom TCP scan from your own flag set.

options.name: -sI
options.summary: Idle (zombie) scan: probes appear to come from another host.

options.name: -sY
options.summary: SCTP INIT scan.

options.name: -sZ
options.summary: SCTP COOKIE-ECHO scan.

options.name: -sO
options.summary: IP protocol scan: which IP protocols (TCP, ICMP, GRE…) the host supports.

options.name: -b
options.summary: FTP bounce scan through a misconfigured FTP server.

options.name: -p
options.summary: Scan exactly these ports.

options.name: -F
options.summary: Fast: only the 100 most common ports.

options.name: --top-ports
options.summary: Scan the N most common ports.

options.name: --port-ratio
options.summary: Scan ports more common than this ratio.

options.name: --exclude-ports
options.summary: Never scan these ports.

options.name: -r
options.summary: Scan ports in order instead of randomizing.

options.name: -sV
options.summary: Probe open ports to identify the service and its version.

options.name: --version-intensity
options.summary: How many probes -sV tries per port (0–9).

options.name: --version-light
options.summary: Quicker, less thorough version detection (intensity 2).

options.name: --version-all
options.summary: Try every version probe (intensity 9).

options.name: --allports
options.summary: Don't skip any port during -sV (by default printer ports like 9100 are skipped).

options.name: --version-trace
options.summary: Debug output for version detection.

options.name: -sC
options.summary: Run the default script set (same as --script=default).

options.name: --script
options.summary: Scripts, categories or boolean expressions. The script browser fills this in.

options.name: --script-args
options.summary: Arguments for the selected scripts (key=value, comma-separated).

options.name: --script-args-file
options.summary: Read script arguments from a file.

options.name: --script-timeout
options.summary: Stop any script that runs longer than this.

options.name: --script-trace
options.summary: Show all data scripts send and receive.

options.name: -O
options.summary: Guess the operating system from TCP/IP fingerprinting.

options.name: -A
options.summary: Aggressive: -O, -sV, -sC and --traceroute in one flag.

options.name: --osscan-limit
options.summary: Only fingerprint hosts with at least one open and one closed port.

options.name: --osscan-guess
options.summary: Report near-matches when there's no exact OS fingerprint.

options.name: --max-os-tries
options.summary: Retries per host for OS detection.

options.name: -T
options.summary: Timing template: T3 is the default, T4 suits fast reliable networks, T0–T1 evade IDS (very slowly).

options.name: --min-rate
options.summary: Send at least this many packets per second.

options.name: --max-rate
options.summary: Send at most this many packets per second.

options.name: --host-timeout
options.summary: Give up on a host after this long.

options.name: --max-retries
options.summary: Cap probe retransmissions per port.

options.name: --scan-delay
options.summary: Wait at least this long between probes.

options.name: --max-scan-delay
options.summary: Never wait longer than this between probes.

options.name: --min-hostgroup
options.summary: Scan at least this many hosts in parallel.

options.name: --max-hostgroup
options.summary: Scan at most this many hosts in parallel.

options.name: --min-parallelism
options.summary: Keep at least this many probes in flight.

options.name: -M
options.summary: Keep at most this many probes in flight (--max-parallelism).

options.name: --initial-rtt-timeout
options.summary: Starting probe timeout.

options.name: --min-rtt-timeout
options.summary: Lowest probe timeout.

options.name: --max-rtt-timeout
options.summary: Highest probe timeout.

options.name: --defeat-rst-ratelimit
options.summary: Don't slow down for hosts that rate-limit RSTs (may mark some closed ports filtered).

options.name: --defeat-icmp-ratelimit
options.summary: Don't slow down for ICMP rate limits during UDP scans (may label some closed ports open|filtered).

options.name: --nsock-engine
options.summary: Force nmap's I/O engine (troubleshooting).

options.name: -f
options.summary: Fragment probes into 8-byte IP fragments.

options.name: -ff
options.summary: Fragment probes into 16-byte IP fragments.

options.name: --mtu
options.summary: Fragment with a custom MTU.

options.name: -D
options.summary: Hide the scan among decoy source addresses.

options.name: -S
options.summary: Spoof the source IP address (replies go to that address).

options.name: -e
options.summary: Send packets from this network interface.

options.name: -g
options.summary: Use this source port (some firewalls trust 53 or 20).

options.name: --proxies
options.summary: Relay TCP connections through HTTP/SOCKS4 proxies (connect scans and scripts only).

options.name: --data
options.summary: Append custom hex bytes to probes.

options.name: --data-string
options.summary: Append a custom string to probes.

options.name: --data-length
options.summary: Pad probes with random bytes.

options.name: --ip-options
options.summary: Send packets with these IP options (record route, source routing…).

options.name: --ttl
options.summary: Set the IP time-to-live.

options.name: --spoof-mac
options.summary: Spoof the source MAC address (0 = random).

options.name: --badsum
options.summary: Send probes with bad checksums (anything that answers isn't checking them, e.g. a firewall).

options.name: --randomize-hosts
options.summary: Scan targets in random order.

options.name: --open
options.summary: Only report open (or possibly open) ports.

options.name: --reason
options.summary: Record why nmap decided each port's state.
Scan IPv6 targets.

options.name: -v
options.summary: Verbose: more detail in nmap's own output.

options.name: -d
options.summary: Debugging output.

options.name: --packet-trace
options.summary: Show every packet sent and received.

options.name: --privileged
options.summary: Assume full raw-socket privileges (use only if nmap really has them, e.g. via setcap).

options.name: --unprivileged
options.summary: Assume no raw-socket privileges.

options.name: --send-eth
options.summary: Send raw Ethernet frames.

options.name: --send-ip
options.summary: Send raw IP packets instead of Ethernet frames.

options.name: --datadir
options.summary: Use nmap data files (services, scripts, fingerprints) from this directory.

options.name: --servicedb
options.summary: Use a custom services file.

options.name: --versiondb
options.summary: Use a custom service-probes file.
